title: mg.start
description: host → server → client (relayed unchanged). The host starts a minigame run on every player phone. Phones load the minigame, answer mg.ready, show the one-sentence instruction and demo until startAtMs, then run it locally from seed and params and report one mg.result. The host is in bullet-time meanwhile. When audience is true spectators receive it too and may play for fun; they report nothing.

runId.description: New run id, never used before in this room.

seed.description: Seed for the local random generator; the same on every phone.

startAtMs.description: Server clock when play begins. Must be at least 3000 ms after sending, for the instruction and demo (§10.1 rule 4).

durationMs.description: Length of play in milliseconds (15–45 s by design).

assistLevel.description: Difficulty the minigame scales with (§10.1 rule 6).

flightPhase.description: Flight phase it belongs to; null for build-phase and debrief minigames.

audience.description: True to deliver the run to spectators as well.

assignments.description: Per-player pieces for COOP_SPLIT, RELAY and TEAM_SYNC; empty for PARALLEL_SOLO. Players not listed play with `params` only.

index.description: Position of the player in the task split or relay order, 0-based. RELAY: the player's turn starts at `startAtMs + index × params.turnMs`.

params.description: Parameters for this player only (their piece of the task).

DataId.description: Identifier of an entry in the shared game data (`data/`): part, part category, contract, test, anomaly card, minigame, fact, codex entry, callout, console request, award, objective, validation rule, cosmetic. 1–48 characters.

FlightPhase.description: Flight phase (§9.1). F0–F1 belong to COUNTDOWN, F2–F13 to FLIGHT. The parallel booster-return track F7b is signalled by `boosterTrack`, not by a value here; F14 is the DEBRIEF phase.

MgMap.description: Open key/value bag for minigame parameters and shared state. Keys and meanings are defined per minigame in `data/minigames.json`; the server relays it without interpretation. At most 32 keys.

PlayerId.description: Player identifier, unique within a room and never reused: "p" followed by a positive integer (p1, p2, …).

RunId.description: Minigame run identifier chosen by the host; unique within the room.

TimeMs.description: Absolute time on the server clock: integer milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Every `…AtMs` field in the protocol uses the server clock (see Clock).
